memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The western boundary is the coastline of the Mediterranean Sea. These are the boundaries around the people of Judah by their clans - Josh 15:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The long tracing of Judah's borders comes to rest with a simple summary: the great sea forms the western edge, and "these are the boundaries around the people of Judah." The map is complete. The inheritance is fully defined, surrounded on every side by borders God Himself has set. Judah now has a home, hemmed in by the care of God.

There is a settledness in that word "around." Judah was not exposed on every side with no protection; they were bounded, contained, given a defined place within which to live and flourish. Boundaries are not only limits — they are also a form of security. A people with borders is a people with a home.

We often chafe against the boundaries in our lives, wishing for fewer limits and more freedom. But God's boundaries around us are as much for our protection as our restriction. The psalmist could say with gratitude, "The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; surely I have a delightful inheritance" (Ps 16:6). To rest within God-given limits is to rest in His care. And our truest security is that we are surrounded by God Himself — He hems us in behind and before, and lays His hand upon us (Ps 139:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you view the boundaries in your life as protection or only as restriction?
- How does it comfort you to know God surrounds His people on every side?
- What would it mean to rest gratefully within the limits God has given you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You surround me on every side. Help me to see Your boundaries as protection and to rest gratefully in the place You have given me. Amen.
